title: Arjuna's praise and his plea for the gentle form

verses.sa: अर्जुन उवाचस्थाने हृषीकेश तव प्रकीर्त्याजगत् प्रहृष्यत्यनुरज्यते च । रक्षांसि भीतानि दिशो द्रवन्तिसर्वे नमस्यन्ति च सिद्धसङ्घाः ॥
verses.tr: Arjuna says: O Hrishikesha, by chanting Your names and glories, the whole world rejoices and becomes devoted. By that chanting, frightened beings flee in all directions, and all the perfected ones bow to You. This is only fitting.
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna has stopped arguing and is overwhelmed. Listen to the single word he uses to describe why Krishna's glory makes the perfected ones bow.

body.text: Arjuna says: O Hrishikesha, by chanting Your names and glories, the whole world rejoices and becomes devoted. By that chanting, frightened beings flee in all directions, and all the perfected ones bow to You. This is only fitting. Listen to the word sthane, which means fittingly. Arjuna is not surprised that the perfected ones bow; he says it is only right and proper that they do so. Arjuna now asks why the perfected beings would not bow to Krishna, the greatest teacher.

verses.sa: कस्माच्च ते न नमेरन्महात्मन्गरीयसे ब्रह्मणोऽप्यादिकर्त्रे । अनन्त देवेश जगन्निवासत्वमक्षरं सदसत्तत्परं यत् ॥
verses.tr: O great one, why would the perfected beings not bow to you, the greatest teacher, the first maker even of Brahma? Endless Lord of radiant beings, abode of the world, you are the imperishable, the real and the unreal, and beyond both.
verses.angle: Arjuna asks why perfected beings would not bow
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: After seeing the cosmic form, Arjuna's fear turns to awe. He asks why perfected beings would not bow to the one who created even Brahma.

body.text: O great one, why would the perfected beings not bow to you, the greatest teacher, the first maker even of Brahma? Endless Lord of radiant beings, abode of the world, you are the imperishable, the real and the unreal, and beyond both. Arjuna asks why perfected beings would not bow to the first maker even of Brahma, and then names you as the imperishable, the real and the unreal, and what lies beyond both. He then calls you the knower and the knowable, the supreme refuge of the entire world.

verses.sa: त्वमादिदेवः पुरुषः पुराणस्त्वमस्य विश्वस्य परं निधानम् । वेत्तासि वेद्यं च परं च धामत्वया ततं विश्वमनन्तरूप ॥
verses.tr: You are the first divine presence, the ancient person, the supreme refuge of this universe. You are the knower, the knowable, and the highest abode. O infinite one, the whole world is pervaded by you.
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Carrying on from his praise of Krishna as the first maker, Arjuna now names the ancient person who is the highest refuge.

body.text: You are the first divine presence, the ancient person, the supreme refuge of this universe. You are the knower, the knowable, and the highest abode. O infinite one, the whole world is pervaded by you. Arjuna calls him the ancient person, the supreme person, the knower, and the knowable, saying the whole world is pervaded by him. He sees Krishna as both the one who knows and the one who is known. He then names Krishna as the wind, fire, the moon, and the great ancestors, bowing again and again.

verses.sa: वायुर्यमोऽग्निर्वरुणः शशाङ्कःप्रजापतिस्त्वं प्रपितामहश्च । नमो नमस्तेऽस्तु सहस्रकृत्वःपुनश्च भूयोऽपि नमो नमस्ते ॥
verses.tr: You are air, Yama, fire, Varuna, the moon, Prajapati, and the great ancestor. I bow to you a thousand times, and again and again.
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: After seeing the cosmic form, Arjuna names the forces of nature and bows again and again. Listen to how he addresses the Lord.

body.text: You are air, Yama, fire, Varuna, the moon, Prajapati, and the great ancestor. I bow to you a thousand times, and again and again. The word pratapamahatvam in the next verse points to boundless power, but here Arjuna fixes his gaze on the great ancestor, the source of Brahma, showing that the creator and the destroyer are one. Arjuna bows to this boundless power from every direction, acknowledging that it is all around him.

verses.sa: नमः पुरस्तादथ पृष्ठतस्तेनमोऽस्तु ते सर्वत एव सर्व । अनन्तवीर्यामितविक्रमस्त्वंसर्वं समाप्नोषि ततोऽसि सर्वः ॥
verses.tr: Salutations to you from the front, from behind, and from every side. You are endless power and immeasurable might; you pervade all and therefore are all.
verses.angle: Every direction is a direction of salutation
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna has just seen the cosmic form, and his body bows to every side. Listen to how he names the directions.

body.text: Salutations to you from the front, from behind, and from every side. You are endless power and immeasurable might; you pervade all and therefore are all. The word purastat means from the front, and prishthatah means from behind. By naming front and behind, Arjuna shows that no direction exists where Krishna is not. Arjuna now admits he has treated Krishna like an equal friend, and he asks forgiveness for his disrespect.

verses.sa: सखेति मत्वा प्रसभं यदुक्तंहे कृष्ण हे यादव हे सखेति । अजानता महिमानं तवेदंमया प्रमादात्प्रणयेन वापि ॥
verses.tr: Thinking of you as a friend, I addressed you carelessly: “O Krishna, O Yadava, O friend.” Not knowing your greatness, I spoke in negligence or affection. I ask forgiveness from your immeasurable form for every disrespect I showed in laughter, play, walking, sleeping, sitting, eating, alone or before companions and relatives.
verses.angle: Calling you friend, not knowing your greatness
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna is overwhelmed, and he names the exact words he used to call his friend. Listen for how he asks for forgiveness.

body.text: Thinking of you as a friend, I addressed you carelessly: “O Krishna, O Yadava, O friend.” Not knowing your greatness, I spoke in negligence or affection. I ask forgiveness from your immeasurable form for every disrespect I showed in laughter, play, walking, sleeping, sitting, eating, alone or before companions and relatives. "O Krishna, O Yadava, O friend": Arjuna remembers calling him these names casually and now asks forgiveness. He now asks for forgiveness for every careless and disrespectful word he has ever spoken to you.

verses.tr: Whatever disrespect I showed you in jest, while walking, resting, sitting, eating, alone or before others, I ask your immeasurable forgiveness.
verses.angle: Arjuna asks for forgiveness for every slight
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna has just seen the universal form and now confesses all his casual slights. Listen to how he names his own carelessness.

body.text: Whatever disrespect I showed you in jest, while walking, resting, sitting, eating, alone or before others, I ask your immeasurable forgiveness. Listen to the word ekah, alone. Arjuna asks for forgiveness for both private errors and public ones, showing he holds nothing back before the divine form. Arjuna now calls Krishna the supreme object of reverence, the greatest teacher, and the father of all beings.

verses.sa: पितासि लोकस्य चराचरस्यत्वमस्य पूज्यश्च गुरुर्गरीयान् । न त्वत्समोऽस्त्यभ्यधिकः कुतोऽन्योलोकत्रयेऽप्यप्रतिमप्रभाव ॥
verses.tr: You are the father of all moving and unmoving beings, the highest object of reverence, and the greatest teacher. In the three worlds, no one equals you, much less surpasses you.
verses.angle: Recognition of the highest power dissolves all comparison.
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna apologizes for his familiar ways, then names the supreme source behind all existence. Listen to how he defines the Lord.

body.text: You are the father of all moving and unmoving beings, the highest object of reverence, and the greatest teacher. In the three worlds, no one equals you, much less surpasses you. Arjuna names Krishna as the father, the greatest teacher, and the unmatched power. He states that in the three worlds, no one equals him, much less surpasses him. Arjuna bows, seeking to please the Lord of praise, and asks for forgiveness as a father forgives a son.

verses.sa: तस्मात्प्रणम्य प्रणिधाय कायंप्रसादये त्वामहमीशमीड्यम् । पितेव पुत्रस्य सखेव सख्युःप्रियः प्रियायार्हसि देव सोढुम् ॥
verses.tr: Therefore, bowing down my body, I seek to please You, the worthy Lord of praise. Like a father bearing a son’s fault, a friend bearing a friend’s, or a lover bearing a beloved’s, You should forgive what I have done.
verses.angle: Sakhya: the bond of friendship Arjuna fears breaking
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna has just seen the universe inside Krishna's body and now begs for mercy. Listen for the three relationships he uses to ask for forgiveness.

body.text: Therefore, bowing down my body, I seek to please You, the worthy Lord of praise. Like a father bearing a son’s fault, a friend bearing a friend’s, or a lover bearing a beloved’s, You should forgive what I have done. The word sakhya means of a friend, and Arjuna places his body down to plead. He asks Krishna to forgive him as a friend forgives a friend, as a father forgives a son, and as a lover forgives a beloved, revealing the deep personal bond Arjuna fears he has broken. Arjuna admits his mind is filled with fear, and he asks to see Krishna's gentle form once more.

verses.sa: अदृष्टपूर्वं हृषितोऽस्मि दृष्ट्वाभयेन च प्रव्यथितं मनो मे । तदेव मे दर्शय देव रूपंप्रसीद देवेश जगन्निवास ॥
verses.tr: I have never seen this form before. Seeing it, I am filled with joy, yet my mind is troubled by fear. Show me again your gentle divine form; be pleased, O Lord of lords, O dwelling of the world.
verses.angle: joy and fear in the same breath
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna stands before the cosmic form and asks Krishna to show him the gentle one again. Listen for the two feelings that rise in him.

body.text: I have never seen this form before. Seeing it, I am filled with joy, yet my mind is troubled by fear. Show me again your gentle divine form; be pleased, O Lord of lords, O dwelling of the world. Listen to how Arjuna names his two feelings. He is hrsito, delighted, yet his manah, mind, is pravyathita, disturbed. He does not choose between joy and fear; they arrive together. Arjuna asks to see Krishna's crowned form again, with mace and discus in his hands.

verses.sa: किरीटिनं गदिनं चक्रहस्तमिच्छामि त्वां द्रष्टुमहं तथैव । तेनैव रूपेण चतुर्भुजेनसहस्रबाहो भव विश्वमूर्ते ॥
verses.tr: I want to see you again in your crowned form, with mace and discus in your hands. O Thousand-Armed One, O Universal Form, return to that four-armed shape.
verses.angle: Chaturbhuja: the four-armed form Arjuna longs for
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna asks to see a shape he recognizes again. Listen to the contrast between the infinite and the familiar.

body.text: I want to see you again in your crowned form, with mace and discus in your hands. O Thousand-Armed One, O Universal Form, return to that four-armed shape. Listen to the pairing of sahastrabaho, the thousand-armed one, and chaturbhuja, the four-armed one. Arjuna is asking the infinite to shrink back into the shape he can hold in his mind and love. Krishna confirms that no one but Arjuna has ever seen this form, and he then begins to explain it.
